claims.text: The initial refractory high-entropy alloy has no preformed protective oxide scale.
Such alloys typically have modest or absent aluminum content at the surface.
A single-step controlled thermal pre-oxidation treatment can form a thin, continuous Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
A preformed Al2O3 scale will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed protection should operate during a 100-hour exposure at 1000°C in air containing approximately 21% oxygen.
The preformed alumina layer is dense and adherent.
The alumina layer acts as a barrier that retards oxygen diffusion into the underlying alloy.
Alumina is thermodynamically stable at high temperatures.
Reducing oxygen ingress and direct oxygen-substrate interaction limits subsequent oxide-scale growth.
Limiting oxide-scale growth mitigates degradation of the alloy's mechanical properties.
Pre-oxidized samples will have a lower oxidation rate than untreated samples.
Pre-oxidized samples will have lower weight gain than untreated samples after 100 hours at 1000°C in air.
Pre-oxidized samples will exhibit less oxide-scale thickening than untreated samples after 100 hours at 1000°C in air.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys characteristically exhibit high oxidation rates and continuous oxide-scale growth under the stated exposure.
Insufficient aluminum availability can limit formation or effectiveness of the protective alumina layer.
Thermal cycling can cause protective-scale spallation and reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between the scale and substrate can reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
The pre-oxidation temperature, duration, and oxygen partial pressure required for a defect-free adherent alumina layer vary with alloy composition.
